items.title: Unified one-pick model
items.tagline: Puts up one best pick per game so the board is simple and every call gets graded in public.
items.latest: 07-25: live record 72-67-5, +1.14 units, every pick graded in public.
items.detail: One model, one pick per game, no hedging. Every pick lands on the site before first pitch and gets graded when the game ends. The running record is 72-67-5 for +1.14 units — modestly ahead, fully transparent.
items.result: 72-67-5, +1.14u live, graded in public

items.title: Star scale v3.3
items.tagline: Rates each pick 1-5 stars so you can see at a glance how strongly the model likes it.
items.latest: 07-24: v3.3 live — 5 stars now means the top 10% of picks; per-tier records shown on site.
items.detail: Stars are earned, not decorative: 5 stars is reserved for roughly the top 10% of picks by model conviction. The site shows the win-loss record for each star tier separately, so you can judge whether the stars actually mean anything.
items.result: 5-star = top 10% of picks; per-tier records live on site

items.title: Expanded pick band
items.tagline: Lets the model take more of its near-miss picks to see if the wider net wins too.

items.result: Backtest 104-78-4 (+15.7%); live since 07-24, separately graded

items.title: Enriched data layer
items.tagline: Feeds the model everything a sharp bettor would check before a game — umps, bullpens, lineups, parks.
items.latest: 07-22: 161 features flowing nightly, all checked to use only information known before each game.
items.detail: The model now sees 161 pieces of pre-game information: who's umping, how tired each bullpen is, detailed pitcher quality readings, the actual lineups, and how each ballpark plays. Everything is snapshotted as-of game time so the model never peeks at the future.
items.result: 161 as-of pre-game features, leakage-checked, nightly refresh

items.title: Sharp-book feed

items.title: Sweet-spot meta-model (TRUST-A)
items.tagline: Learns when the model tends to be right, so we lean in on its good spots and ease off its bad ones.
items.latest: 2026-07-25: full nested walk-forward eval complete — closed honestly
items.detail: We built a second model to learn WHEN the main model is right. It found a real but tiny trust gradient, and on the strict tests the trust flag was not sharper than the market and leaned too hard to unders. Nothing ships; the record stays clean. It did leave two new doors (see queued items).
items.result: NULL — trust flag failed the market-sharpness gate (and 94.5%-under sidedness); tiny +3.1pt trust gradient real but unbettable

items.title: Mega edge hunt
items.tagline: Runs a huge overnight sweep of 46 candidate betting ideas and fully builds the 12 strongest.
items.latest: 2026-07-26: all 12 fronts complete — zero survivors, nine doors closed for good
items.detail: The biggest sweep we have run: 97 ideas from 25 research angles, narrowed to the 12 strongest, each pre-registered and tested on old data only. Nothing earned money. The recurring lesson: where a retail book looks slow or generous, it is usually informed behavior or noise — and the real patterns we did find were already in the price. One old edge (shopping extreme prices vs the sharpest book) existed but died around 2023.
items.result: 0 of 12 fronts survived; 9 mechanisms permanently closed; banked facts feed future models

items.title: Deep internet research sweep
items.tagline: Sends 24 researchers across the internet to find edges other people have already discovered.
items.latest: 2026-07-26: sweep complete — 213 findings from 25 researchers, distilled to 35 testable ideas
items.detail: Twenty-four research agents fan out tonight across GitHub code, Reddit threads, academic papers, professional bettor lore, and how the betting markets themselves work. Anything promising gets written up as a candidate idea and fed into the edge-hunt pipeline for honest testing.
items.result: 213 findings -> 35-idea testable queue + full sourced dossier; queue now piloting

items.title: Rapid pilot pool
items.tagline: Fires off up to 40 quick, cheap experiments on old seasons to see which ideas deserve a real build.
items.latest: 2026-07-26: all 35 pilots complete — 33 dead, 1 blocked on data, 0 graduated
items.detail: Thirty-five ideas from the internet research sweep got a fast honest trial on old seasons we can afford to burn. None earned the right to touch the good data. Three patterns explain nearly every death: the books already price the effect (weather, umpires, parks, air density); the profit was really just one good season; or the idea only fires 20-80 times a year, too rare to ever prove.
items.result: 0 of 35 graduated; 33 dead, 1 blocked; confirmation data untouched

items.title: Platoon splits data build
items.tagline: Adds how each hitter does against lefty versus righty pitching to the model's information.
items.latest: 2026-07-26: data build finished overnight, real test ran — directionally right, economically inert
items.detail: Do batters facing a badly-matched starter (handedness splits) beat the total? The data build finished after weeks, and the test finally ran on 6,366 games. The tilt exists in the direction we predicted — but it is smaller than the vig, so it does not pay for itself at any book, and it is statistically indistinguishable from noise.
items.result: NULL — 176-game cell, 50.6% hit vs 50.7% break-even, ROI -0.2% (-3.0% at our book); holdout not spent

items.title: NRFI first-inning niche
items.tagline: Tries a specialist model for the popular no-runs-first-inning bet, where our pitcher data may shine.
items.latest: 2026-07-25: full pre-registered test on 5,297 priced games — market wins at the root; door closed
items.detail: The idea: first-inning (NRFI/YRFI) markets get less attention, so maybe they are softer. We built true first-inning pitcher form from pitch-level data and tested honestly on 4,609 out-of-sample games. The books price the first inning slightly BETTER than our data. All six pre-declared cells died. Together with the earlier probe, both natural angles are now closed — no future cycle needs to wonder about NRFI.
items.result: NULL — market Brier beats ours at the root (0.2482 vs 0.2490); 0 of 6 cells survived; last untested derivative niche closed

items.title: Line-divergence direction-only v3
items.tagline: Third try at the disagree-with-Vegas idea, now only trusting the direction of the disagreement, not its size.
items.latest: 2026-07-25: pre-registered test complete — missed the final significance bar by a hair; stop honored
items.detail: Third redesign of the sharp-book disagreement idea. For the first time the mechanism test passed on the numbers, but the family-wide significance bar missed (p=0.071 vs the 0.05 we froze in advance), so the rule says null and we honored it. Notably, on the one book profile Leon can actually bet, every per-cell test passed with +11.5% over 496 games — that thread continues in a redesigned follow-up.
items.result: NULL by pre-registered bar (p=0.071 vs 0.05) — but the bettable-book subset passed every per-cell gate (+11.5%, n=496); holdout stays sealed

items.title: Pinnacle divergence live flags
items.tagline: Quietly flags every game where we disagree with the sharpest book, and counts how often that happens.
items.latest: 07-25: flags recording daily; about a week until we know how often they fire.
items.detail: Every day we log the games where our number disagrees with Pinnacle's. Nothing is bet on these yet — first we need to see how often the flag even fires. About a week of accrual gets us that answer, then we can judge whether the disagreements win.

items.title: Team-total quotes
items.tagline: Collects betting lines on each team's individual run total, a quieter market we may model well.
items.latest: 07-25: quote capture running daily; needs several weeks of history before testing.
items.detail: Team totals — how many runs one team scores, not both combined — are a quieter market that fewer people study. We are capturing the daily quotes now. Testing needs a real sample, so this one is a 4-6 week accumulation before any verdict.

items.title: Weather forecast snapshots
items.tagline: Saves the pre-game weather forecast every day so future models can use wind and heat honestly.
items.latest: 07-25: snapshots growing daily.
items.detail: Wind and temperature move run totals, but to test that honestly you need the forecast as it looked before the game, not the weather that actually happened. We snapshot pre-game forecasts every day. The archive grows daily until it is big enough to test.

items.title: F5 totals model
items.tagline: Asked whether first-five-innings totals were beatable with our approach; the answer was no.
items.latest: 07-06: closed after a full search found zero picks worth taking.
items.detail: We built a dedicated model for first-five-innings totals and searched 25,710 priced rows for bets worth taking. It found zero. Tested honestly, door closed — the books price this market too well for our current tools.
items.result: 0 +EV takes in 25,710 rows

items.title: F5-to-full-game coherence
items.tagline: Checked whether the relationship between first-half and full-game lines hides an edge; it doesn't.
items.latest: 07-06: closed — the two markets move in lockstep with nothing left over.
items.detail: The idea was that first-five lines and full-game lines might drift out of sync in exploitable ways. They don't: the first-five share of the full total sits at a constant 0.586, and none of our features added anything on top. Tested honestly, door closed.
items.result: F5 share constant at 0.586; features add nothing

items.title: Segment mining
items.tagline: Sliced the betting universe into 1,378 situations hunting for pockets where the line is lazy; found none.
items.latest: 07-12: closed — every apparent winner dissolved under honest checking.
items.detail: We carved games into 1,378 situational slices — day games after night games, certain umps, certain parks — looking for pockets the books misprice. Plenty looked like winners at first glance. After correcting for the fact that we checked 1,378 of them, zero survived. Tested honestly, door closed.

items.latest: 07-14: closed — the market already adjusts for resting stars.
items.detail: When a star sits, does the total stay too high? No — the books already move the line by roughly the right amount, about 0.05 runs of pricing that matches the real effect. Nothing left to take. Tested honestly, door closed.

items.title: Sharp-divergence v1/v2
items.tagline: First two tries at betting our disagreements with sharp books; profitable in the lab but not trustworthy.
items.latest: 07-24: closed — it made money in development but failed the believability test.
items.detail: Both versions showed a profit in development, which is exactly when to be most suspicious. The mechanism check failed: our disagreement sizes overshot reality by about 2.5 times, meaning the profit came from overconfidence, not insight. We closed it without touching the holdout data, so a smarter version 3 can still be tested fairly.
items.result: Failed mechanism gate — magnitudes overshoot 2.5x; holdout preserved

items.title: Distrust filter (avoid the worst picks)
items.tagline: Use the meta-model to REMOVE our shakiest picks instead of finding better ones.
items.latest: 2026-07-26: decision brief did the honest math — headline overstated, cannot be proven in a human timeframe
items.detail: The idea: skip our least-trusted picks. On closer inspection the result includes zero in its own error bars, and when transferred to the picks we actually serve it was worth nothing (-0.24pp). Even if real, it is worth about 1 point and would take 7-15 seasons to prove.
items.result: NULL — CI includes zero, transfer test -0.24pp (p=0.53), needs 7-15 seasons to certify

items.title: Big-disagreement region confirm
items.tagline: Independently confirm that our biggest disagreements with Vegas are our most profitable picks.
items.latest: 2026-07-26: turned out to be already shipped — this rule is in production today
items.detail: We thought we had found a contradiction: a region we planned to veto looked profitable. The brief resolved it — the two numbers describe two different models, and the sweet-spot-then-decay pattern was already measured and is already how picks are graded today. Nothing to change.
items.result: Already in production (the conviction sweet spot); the apparent contradiction was two different models being compared

items.title: Sharp-book disagreement (whole family)
items.tagline: Four honest attempts to bet where our book disagrees with the sharpest book. Retired.
items.latest: 2026-07-26: the kill-test came back unproven, and the idea reverses on every book except the one we picked
items.detail: The premise was that our book hangs the stale number and the sharp book knows better. Tested directly on the exact games we would bet: our book was NOT measurably worse. Worse for the thesis, when you look across all bettable books the effect flips sign entirely — it only survives at the single book we had already picked for having the best returns, which is how false edges are born. The apparent signal traced back to one hot 49-bet stretch; remove two seasons and it inverts.
items.result: RETIRED after four honored stops — and the one-shot validation data was never spent

items.title: Tougher standing test gates
items.tagline: Make every future test harder to fool: control comparisons, drop-the-best-bet robustness, per-season honesty.
items.latest: 2026-07-26: shipped with 21/21 tests passing — and it immediately erased a claimed +0.66% that was a measurement artifact

items.title: Two unfinished tests, finished
items.tagline: Completed two experiments whose runs had died mid-flight, so nothing sits ambiguous.

items.detail: Two ideas about our own book being slow or mispricing injury news. Both had stalled on code that never finished running. Fixed and completed. items.title: Serving hardening + record checks
items.tagline: Defused an installer that would have taken down six live jobs, and turned one weak record check into five real ones.
items.latest: 2026-07-26: verified by actually running the installer — it now safely skips healthy jobs
items.detail: Config files in the repo had drifted from what actually runs. Reinstalling would have broken six jobs two different ways: three crash on startup, three more write logs somewhere background jobs are not allowed. Separately, a failing record check turned out not to be a grading bug — two ledgers were counting different populations — so it was replaced with five sharper checks that name the offending game if a real gap ever appears.
items.result: Installer safe and idempotent; record selftests 48 pass/1 fail -> 56 pass/0 fail

items.title: Does knowing the lineup help?
items.tagline: We cheated on purpose: handed the model the real batting order it could never know, and measured what it was worth.
items.latest: 2026-07-26: worth about nothing — and the market is just as accurate three hours before any lineup exists
items.detail: Rather than build better lineup predictions, we gave the model the actual nine hitters from the box score — information no bettor could ever have — across 8,300 games. A better lineup is worth about a quarter of a run raw, but the posted total already knows most of it, and the lineup we can project the day before captures ninety percent of the rest. What is genuinely new when the lineup posts moves the game by about a fiftieth of a run, and the book prices even that. Decisive check: the market forecasts just as well at six hours out, when zero lineups have posted, as at one hour out when nearly all have.
items.result: NULL — actual-vs-projected lineup worth +0.019 runs (CI includes zero); 0 of 33 tests beat the market; best honest ROI +0.02%
